nodes.label: PlanBench-XL Benchmark
nodes.rationale: Interactive benchmark for evaluating LLM agents' long-horizon planning in large-scale, retrieval-mediated tool ecosystems with 327 retail tasks over 1,665 tools.

nodes.label: Typed Tool Library Construction
nodes.rationale: Systematic generation of 1,665 tools from 56 datatypes via LLM-proposed tool functionalities filtered for redundancy and realism; includes noisy tools simulating real-world ecosystem distractors.

nodes.label: Backend Database with Concrete Values
nodes.rationale: Instantiated retail records with non-trivial values that cannot be inferred from common sense; tool responses match input arguments to records and return output datatype values.

nodes.label: Query Generation Pipeline
nodes.rationale: Three-step process: (1) specify task as (initial_datatypes, target_datatypes), (2) compute ground-truth tool-call sequences via state graph reachability, (3) instantiate and verbalize as natural-language query with ground-truth answer.

nodes.label: Bi-directional Tool Retrieval
nodes.rationale: Three retrieval modes: (1) input-conditioned (forward anticipation from available evidence), (2) output-conditioned (backward anticipation from desired outcome), (3) input-output-conditioned (constrained search).

nodes.label: Retrieval-Time Blocking Module
nodes.rationale: Optional perturbation replacing path-critical tools with three failure types: explicit errors, implicit failures (silent wrong values), semantic misleading tools; preserves solvability via alternative paths.

nodes.label: Agent State Definition
nodes.rationale: Latent state (query, discovered_tools, obtained_datatypes) maintained by environment; tracks progress across tool calls but not directly visible to agent.

nodes.label: Evaluation Metrics Suite
nodes.rationale: Seven metrics: accuracy, EGT precision (task-relevant execution), average turns, mean explored datatypes, search-to-call ratio, invalid tool call rate, untrusted input rejection rate.

nodes.label: Frontier LLM Evaluation
nodes.rationale: Tested 10 models: GPT-5.4 (51.90% accuracy), Gemini-3.1-Pro (77.06%), DeepSeek-V4-Flash (63.08%), Llama-3.3-70B (18.96%), Qwen3 variants (0-2.75%); shows massive-tool planning remains challenging.

nodes.label: Trajectory Drift Failure Mode
nodes.rationale: Models make partial progress then drift away from valid solution paths via non-progress tool calls; recovery is rare (3% of failures), indicating weak adaptive re-planning.

nodes.label: Tool Selection Failure Analysis
nodes.rationale: 78% of failed non-progress calls occur despite useful alternatives already retrieved; models over-select recently retrieved tools (74.1%) even when older tools would advance the task.

nodes.label: Silent Failure Vulnerability
nodes.rationale: Implicit failures (silent wrong values) most harmful: 42.2% value reuse vs 0% for explicit errors; agents treat invalid values as grounded evidence, propagating failures downstream.

nodes.label: Model-Specific Termination Policies
nodes.rationale: GPT surrenders (77.3%), DeepSeek/Llama commit hallucinated values (58-81%), Gemini exhausts search (90.8%); patterns stable across settings, indicating hierarchical failure structure.

nodes.label: Blocking Severity Analysis
nodes.rationale: GPT-5.4 accuracy drops from 51.90% (no block) to 11.36% (longest-path-only block); longer recovery paths especially difficult; enforced exploration yields <5% gains.

nodes.label: Exploration-Exploitation Trade-off
nodes.rationale: Mean explored datatypes (EDT) strongly correlated with accuracy (r=0.902), but high search-to-call ratio does not guarantee success; Gemini-3.5-Flash searches 10x more than Gemini-3.1-Pro with lower EDT.

nodes.label: Bi-directional Anticipation Importance
nodes.rationale: Output-conditioned (backward) retrieval frequency strongly correlated with accuracy (r=0.800); low-performing models rely heavily on input-conditioned (forward) retrieval, missing backward reasoning.

nodes.label: LLM Agent Planning in Tool Ecosystems
nodes.rationale: Emerging research area: agents must discover relevant tools from large sets, infer implicit subgoals, and adapt to dynamic environments; retrieval-mediated access introduces partial observability and unreliability.
